pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor (Anti-NMDAR) Encephalitis secondary to an ovarian teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of acute psychiatric decline progressing to orofacial dyskinesias and autonomic instability, along with a complex ovarian mass (teratoma) and the pathognomonic extreme delta brush pattern on EEG. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient's ectopic ovarian teratoma contained neural elements expressing GluN1 subunits of the NMDA receptor. This triggered systemic production of pathogenic IgG autoantibodies against these extracellular epitopes. Upon crossing the blood-brain barrier, the antibodies bound to NMDA receptors in the frontostriatal and hippocampal networks, inducing receptor cross-linking and internalization. The resulting loss of cell-surface NMDAR function precipitated severe neuropsychiatric destruction, choreoathetosis, autonomic dysregulation, and central respiratory failure. Treatment mandates immediate surgical resection of the ovarian teratoma combined with high-dose immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG, or plasmapheresis).
